usageNotes: Permanently destroys a ZFS pool on the specified node; the node must be online and the caller must hold Sys.Modify on /. Returns a task UPID — poll the task status endpoint to confirm completion before treating the pool as gone. If the pool is also registered as a Proxmox storage, pass cleanup-config=true to remove or disable that storage entry; without it the storage record remains and will show errors.

examples.summary: Destroy a ZFS pool named 'tank' on node 'pve1', removing its storage config entry and wiping the member disks for reuse

destructiveReason: All data on the ZFS pool is irrecoverably destroyed; if cleanup-disks is set, the underlying disk partitions are also wiped and cannot be recovered.
tips: Poll the returned UPID via GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to detect failures — the DELETE call returns immediately with a task reference, not the final result.
cleanup-config only removes the storage from this node's configuration; if the storage is shared across multiple nodes you may need to remove it cluster-wide via the storage API afterward.
Ensure no VMs or CTs have active disks on this pool before destroying it — Proxmox does not enforce this check automatically.
cleanup-disks performs a partition wipe (dd/blkdiscard) on member vdevs; omit it if you plan to reuse the disks in a new pool with a fresh zpool create.
